or build an archive to distribute through TestFlight or ad hoc:

flutter build ipa --release --dart-define-from-file=dart_defines/store.json

docs.title: Relay with the same project
docs.text:
Deploy the relay as described in Deploy, with the service account JSON from step 5 above as FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT. It must come from the Firebase project in store.json; a service account from any other project cannot send to this build's tokens.

Mint a relay credential. normalizeKey in relay/src/entitlement.ts accepts PH- followed by four groups of four characters from A-Z0-9; the relay compares the SHA-256 hex of the credential against ENTITLEMENT_STATIC_KEYS:

KEY="PH-$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 16 | sed 's/.\{4\}/&-/g;s/-$//')"
echo "$KEY"                                   # goes into the app's relay URL
printf '%s' "$KEY" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1   # goes into ENTITLEMENT_STATIC_KEYS

In relay/wrangler.jsonc:

Field Set to routes remove the entry; it is the project's custom domain. The Worker is then served at <name>.<account>.workers.dev kv_namespaces[0].id the id printed by npx wrangler kv namespace create DENY vars.FCM_PROJECT_ID your Firebase project id, or leave "" to read project_id from the service account vars.ANDROID_PACKAGE your Android applicationId (only used when ATTEST_MODE is android or all) vars.ENTITLEMENT_URL "" unless you run your own entitlement service. The committed value points at the project's service; with that value and an ENTITLEMENT_SECRET set, the relay asks that service and never consults ENTITLEMENT_STATIC_KEYS vars.ENTITLEMENT_STATIC_KEYS the SHA-256 hex from above; several credentials are separated by commas

With ENTITLEMENT_STATIC_KEYS you do not need ENTITLEMENT_SECRET.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. Phone: Settings → Push relay, paste https://<KEY>@<your-worker>.workers.dev.
  2. Each machine: set [push] relay_url to the base URL without the credential and restart the daemon.

Both steps are described in Push notifications.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: "Relay: not active" and the relay log says no entitlement source configured Neither ENTITLEMENT_URL + ENTITLEMENT_SECRET nor ENTITLEMENT_STATIC_KEYS is set (checkEntitlement in relay/src/entitlement.ts). Set ENTITLEMENT_STATIC_KEYS and redeploy. "Relay: not active" and the relay log says unknown credential The credential's hash is not in ENTITLEMENT_STATIC_KEYS, or ENTITLEMENT_URL is still the committed value so the relay asked the project's entitlement service instead. Hash the credential again with printf '%s' (no trailing newline) and check ENTITLEMENT_URL is "". The relay is connected but the daemon log shows push failed with (410) or relay returned 502 The relay could not deliver to the token. It answers 410 push token gone when FCM returns 400 or 404 and 502 fcm <status> for any other FCM error (handlePush in relay/src/index.ts); on 410 the daemon drops the grant for that device. The usual cause is a project mismatch: the app was built with one Firebase project's store.json and the relay's FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT belongs to another. A store build with your own relay fails the same way. Rebuild the app from the project the service account comes from. iOS never gets a push token See "Apple has not issued this phone a push token yet". For a self-built app also confirm the APNs key is uploaded in Cloud Messaging and the App ID has the Push Notifications capability.

docs.title: Self-hosting the push relay
docs.text: The relay is only needed for background push on phones. The app takes any relay URL in Settings → Push relay; the project hosts one for its supporters (https://zerkersec.io/supporter hands out a personal URL; see Push notifications), and this page is how to run your own.

docs.title: The relay URL
docs.text: The app accepts https://[credential@]host[/path]. The optional userinfo is the relay credential: the app sends it as Authorization: Bearer on the grant request and never interprets it. A relay with ENTITLEMENT_STATIC_KEYS hands out credentials of the form PH-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX; a relay backed by an entitlement service uses whatever that service issues. The daemon only needs the base URL (no credential) in [push] relay_url.

docs.title: What it needs
docs.text:
Secret / var Purpose GRANT_SIGNING_KEY Ed25519 private key (PKCS8, base64url) that signs push grants. Generate: node -e "crypto.subtle.generateKey({name:'Ed25519'},true,['sign','verify']).then(async k=>console.log(Buffer.from(await crypto.subtle.exportKey('pkcs8',k.privateKey)).toString('base64url')))" FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT Firebase service account JSON with the Firebase Cloud Messaging API role FCM_PROJECT_ID (var) Firebase project id (optional; read from the service account otherwise) ENTITLEMENT_URL (var) + ENTITLEMENT_SECRET an HTTPS endpoint that answers whether a credential is active (see below) ENTITLEMENT_STATIC_KEYS (var) alternative for a personal relay: comma-separated SHA-256 hex hashes of the credentials you hand out yourself ATTEST_MODE (var) off, android (Play Integrity) or all; iOS App Attest is not yet implemented, so all refuses iOS grants. The store builds send no attestation today, so leave it off for them DENY (KV) revoked device ids and daily counters

Keep the origin of record for every secret outside the repo; set them with wrangler secret put.

The service account must belong to the Firebase project the app was built with: push tokens are issued per project, and the relay can only send to tokens of the project it holds a service account for. The store builds carry the project's own Firebase options, so they only work with the hosted relay. To use your own relay, build the app with your own project.

docs.title: The entitlement contract
docs.text: The relay never decides who may push. It calls POST $ENTITLEMENT_URL with Authorization: Bearer $ENTITLEMENT_SECRET and body {"key": "<credential>", "device_id": "...", "platform": "ios|android"} and expects {"active": true|false, "period_end": "<ISO 8601>", "level": 0, "tier": null, "reason": "..."}. level and tier are optional: a tier level (1 and up) and its name, passed back to the app on the grant response. Omit them or send 0 for a flat yes/no. Status 404 means unknown credential, 429 means too many devices on that credential. The grant it mints expires at period_end or 30 days, whichever is sooner, and the app re-mints within three days of expiry, so revoking a credential on your side takes effect by the next refresh. Any backend that follows this contract works; Porthole's own is the supporter service at zerkersec.io.

docs.title: Deploy
docs.text:
cd relay
npm install
npx wrangler kv namespace create DENY     # put the id into wrangler.jsonc
# remove the "routes" entry in wrangler.jsonc (it is the project's custom domain)
npx wrangler secret put GRANT_SIGNING_KEY
npx wrangler secret put FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT
npx wrangler secret put ENTITLEMENT_SECRET   # or set ENTITLEMENT_STATIC_KEYS as a var
npx wrangler deploy

Then build the app with the same Firebase project, paste https://<credential>@your-worker.workers.dev into Settings → Push relay, and set [push] relay_url in the daemon config to the base URL.

docs.title: How a push travels
docs.text:
1. The user pastes a relay URL into the app, which obtains a platform push token from FCM.
  2. The app asks the relay for a grant: POST /v1/grant with the credential as a bearer token. The relay asks the entitlement service whether it is active and returns a signed grant binding the device id and push token, valid for at most 30 days.
  3. The app hands the grant to each paired daemon over the VPN.
  4. When a session needs you and the phone is not connected, the daemon encrypts a notice with the key agreed at pairing and posts {grant, ct} to the relay.
  5. The relay checks the signature, expiry, deny list and rate limits, then sends the ciphertext through FCM. The phone decrypts it and shows the notification, and the app fetches details from the daemon on open.

The relay never sees session content, repository names or prompts. It sees a push token, a device id and a timestamp.

docs.title: Blocking a device
docs.text: npx wrangler kv key put --binding DENY <device-id> 1

docs.title: Rotating the grant key
docs.text: Set a new GRANT_SIGNING_KEY; existing grants stop verifying immediately and apps re-mint on their next refresh (within three days of a grant's expiry).
